items.title: Today in Apple history: Apple Park gets the official go-ahead
items.snippet: November 19, 2013: Apple gets final approval from the Cupertino City Council to proceed with building a massive second campus to house the iPhone-maker’s growing army of workers in California. Regarding the company’s new headquarters, which ultimately will be named Apple Park, Cupertino Mayor Orrin Mahoney issues a simple message: “Go for it.” However, the massive structure — with an innovative circular design that will earn it the nickname “the spaceship” — remains years away from opening, despite Apple’s ambitious schedule. Apple CEO Steve Jobs didn’t just want a bigger office for his company. He wanted a headquarters that would embody Apple’s ambitions, down to the smallest architectural detail. The sprawling circular campus now known as Apple Park was one of Jobs’ final obsessions — a $4 billion monument to his belief that great design could transform even the places where people work. items.snippet: Windows 11 Insider Preview Build 26320.10003 on the Beta channel now lets standard users assign a BitLocker preboot PIN to the operating system drive. Until this change, only administrators could add the TPM+PIN protector, which made preboot authentication awkward to roll out on PCs where users lack admin rights. You turn the capability on with four existing BitLocker CSP policies in Intune or another MDM. This piece covers how the feature behaves, how you configure it, and which limits apply while you test. Source

items.title: What is Microsoft Perception?
items.snippet: Microsoft Perception is an AI security layer that routes specialized agents to spot weaknesses, investigate incidents, and recommend or help execute remediations. It rides on Microsoft Defender and draws signals and controls from Intune, Entra, Sentinel, and Purview. General availability landed at Ignite on November 17, 2026, but several features—including much of the Intune path—are still in preview. Source

items.title: Windows 11 hotpatch breaks Office apps; Microsoft offers registry workaround

items.title: Windows 11 update reportedly removes webcam zoom controls on Lenovo laptops

items.title: PHP fixes seven critical flaws, including phpAfterShell RCE
items.snippet: PHP has released fixes for seven critical vulnerabilities, including the previously announced CVE-2026-115560 remote code execution flaw . Another flaw, dubbed phpAfterShell, can turn corrupted session files into a path to code execution. The fixes are available in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6.0; the release also addresses a high-severity local privilege escalation issue. Source

items.title: Critical VMware vCenter login bypass demands emergency patching
items.snippet: Broadcom has released emergency fixes for a critical VMware vCenter flaw that lets network attackers bypass authentication. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-123890, affects the central management console for ESX hosts and virtual machines. Broadcom lists no workaround. Source

items.title: Windows 11 26H2 automatic rollout starts for unmanaged 24H2 and 25H2 PCs
items.snippet: Microsoft has begun automatically delivering Windows 11 26H2 to eligible, unmanaged PCs running versions 24H2 and 25H2. The November 18 expansion follows the update’s availability through manual checks in late October. Automatic delivery does not necessarily mean immediate installation without user interaction. Source

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon beats Carbon on benchmarks, but its savings depend on pricing
items.snippet: Gemini 4 Neon is Google’s cloud-based AI model for coding, analysis, and enterprise workflows. New benchmark comparisons show that the recently launched model can outperform Gemini 4 Carbon while completing some tasks faster and at a lower regular price. But Neon’s savings come from cheaper tokens, not necessarily fewer of them. Source

items.title: Microsoft Edge Lockdown Mode now blocks WebGL and WebGPU in Canary
items.snippet: Microsoft is testing Edge Lockdown Mode, a browser security feature that blocks graphics APIs to reduce exposure to targeted attacks. The Canary experiment adds protections to an experimental flag that previously had no active safeguards . The trade-off is that some websites may stop working correctly. Source

items.title: Windows 11 26H2 now rolls out automatically to more PCs
items.snippet: Microsoft has begun automatically delivering Windows 11 26H2 to eligible unmanaged PCs, so users no longer need to check for the update manually. The rollout began November 18, after 26H2 became available to eligible Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2 devices in late October. Source

items.title: Copilot will diagnose Windows 11 faults and suggest fixes
items.snippet: Microsoft plans to give Copilot the ability to scan Windows 11 PCs for problems and suggest fixes, without making the repairs itself. The announced feature will use a local, read-only scan to investigate issues such as incorrect audio routing. Microsoft has not announced a release date or complete hardware requirements. Source

items.title: Database RCE proof-of-concept exploits hit PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle without broad privileges
items.snippet: New proof-of-concept exploits show that restricted database accounts can run code on PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse servers. A separate Oracle Database exploit chain reportedly requires no login at all. Fixes are available for the Oracle, PostgreSQL and MySQL flaws, but no fixed ClickHouse version has been confirmed. Source

items.title: Microsoft brings local AI inference to Windows Server with AMD MI350P
items.snippet: Microsoft plans to bring AI inference closer to enterprise data on Windows Server, with AMD Instinct MI350P support for Windows Server 2025 and 2028. The accelerator is scheduled to enter preview in the first half of 2027. Source

items.title: Old Windows bug linked to theft of 1 million payment cards from POS terminals
items.snippet: An exposed attacker server has revealed the theft of at least one million credit and debit card records from Windows point-of-sale (POS) terminals. The campaign affected more than 700 terminals in over 20 countries, with most infections in Brazil. The attacker exploited CVE-2024-49138, a Windows vulnerability patched in December 2024. Source

items.title: AI agents borrow employee credentials and leave gaps in audit logs
items.snippet: AI agents built into everyday business tools often inherit their creators’ access without appearing as separate identities, a Nudge Security report finds. Among its customers with at least one agent, the median organization had seven, and 44% had more than 10. The findings come from anonymized customer telemetry, not a representative survey of all organizations. Source

items.title: Entra ID brings back memberOf for dynamic groups with a new licensing requirement
items.snippet: Microsoft Entra ID has introduced MemberOf Next in public preview, restoring a way to build dynamic groups from other groups’ members. The replacement arrives after the original memberOf rules stopped updating on November 3, 2026. A second preview operator, Transitive Reports To, builds groups from a manager’s reporting hierarchy. Source

items.title: Outages in the US are not caused by AI, but rather by humans who are anxious about its potential
items.snippet: Journalist Garrett Graff, former CISA director Jen Easterly, and cybersecurity journalist Nicole Perlroth discuss a series of US technology outages and their implications for critical infrastructure. Officials said they had found no evidence that the disruptions were connected or caused by cyberattacks. The guests examine whether AI-driven vulnerability discovery and pressure to patch fragile systems could contribute to future disruptions. Source

items.snippet: Broadcom has released patches for bugs in multiple products, one of which, fixing a VMware vCenter authentication bypass vulnerability, is rated 9.8 out of 10 in severity. It advises immediate patching. Broadcom has provided fixed vCenter versions 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, and 8.0 U3m; customers running v7.0 will only get a patch if they have an extended support contract. items.title: StarlingX 13.0 updates the network stack for distributed edge deployments
items.snippet: Edge sites do not always come with the network gear that a data center takes for granted. That’s a challenge the open-source StarlingX project from the OpenInfra Foundation is now tackling in its 13.0 update. StarlingX is an open-source distributed cloud platform that combines Linux, Kubernetes, OpenStack, and Ceph. The OpenInfra Foundation hosts the project, and operators including Verizon, Vodafone, T-Systems and KDDI use it for 5G and Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) infrastructure. Earlier this year, the StarlingX 12.0 update added precision timing capabilities to help networking stay on time. The 13.0 update tackles a different set of issues. Key features include: Gateway API support.

items.title: Sovereign AI is about control, not just location

items.title: You’ve decided to repatriate cloud workloads. Now what?
items.snippet: For 15 years, enterprise IT moved in one direction: out of the data center and into the public cloud. Hardware teams were trimmed, leases weren’t renewed, and “cloud first” became “cloud only.” That era is ending, not because the cloud failed, but because many organizations never made a placement decision.
